entries.title: History and culture
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or recently active items relevant to the River Brain, all from the last ~30 days or clearly post-August 1, 2026 baseline where noted:

---

- 
**Grand River Bands 44th Annual Homecoming of the Three Fires**, June 13-14, 2026, Riverside Park, Grand Rapids: two days of traditional Ottawa cultural programming hosted by the Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians. (Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians website, June 12, 2026)


- 
**H.R. 3255, the Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians Restoration Act of 2025**, remains active in the 119th Congress. The bill affirms federal recognition and eligibility for federal services, with a defined service area of Newaygo, Oceana, Kent, Muskegon, and Ottawa Counties. (Congress.gov, 119th Congress, 2025-2026)
 
A companion Senate bill, S. 2160, has also been introduced in the same session. (Congress.gov, 2025-2026)


- 
**New book published:** *The Historical Archaeology of Michigan* by Dean L. Anderson, Michael S. Nassaney, and Krysta Ryzewski, University Press of Florida, published January 13, 2026, 276 pages. The book covers 400 years of archaeological research in Michigan, including themes of colonization, the fur trade, and land acquisition relevant to the Grand River corridor. (Amazon/University Press of Florida, January 2026)


- 
The new book's findings associated with **Anishinaabe peoples, settler colonialism, immigrants, agriculture, industry, and urbanization** illustrate distinct dimensions of Michigan experience, with direct relevance to Grand River Valley contexts. (Project MUSE, 2026)


- 
The **Grand Rapids Public Museum** is currently running the planetarium show *Anishinaabe Star Knowledge* alongside other exhibits in summer 2026, connecting Indigenous cultural heritage to public programming at the river's edge. (GRPM website, accessed July 28, 2026)


---

No major new archaeological discoveries, archival releases, or documentaries specifically about the Grand River corridor were found published within the last 30 days. The items above represent the most recent developments surfaced by this search.

entries.title: Development and funding
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since early July 2026):

---

- 
**July 22, 2026:** Gov. Whitmer signed Senate Bill 723 (Public Act 36 of 2026), revising the state's Transformational Brownfield Program by expanding oversight, tying tax reimbursements to measurable project performance, and raising the incentive capacity for future projects.
 
The law roughly doubles the program's annual capacity, authorizing an additional $80 million in state tax capture and raising the yearly ceiling to as much as $160 million, with the total aggregate cap rising to roughly $3.2 billion.
 
State officials cited stalled projects including riverfront work in Grand Rapids as examples of the capacity constraints the law is meant to relieve.
 (Environment+Energy Leader, July 30, 2026)

- 
**July 30, 2026:** MDOT announced approximately $4.6 million in Transportation Alternatives Program grants for three West Michigan projects, including $1.7 million to the Ottawa County Road Commission for separated pathway construction in the Allendale segment of the Grand River Greenway Trail.
 (WHTC, July 30, 2026)

- 
**July 14, 2026:** Crain's Grand Rapids Business reported new state funding for the Transformational Brownfield Program is expected to advance major waterfront developments in Grand Rapids, Muskegon, and Holland.
 (Crain's Grand Rapids Business, July 14, 2026)

- 
**June 2026** (confirmed within last ~3 weeks): The Grand River Restoration, Lower Reach, broke ground, with construction now underway on the stretch extending from Fulton Street to Bridge Street in the heart of downtown.
 (Experience Grand Rapids, ~July 2026)

- 
**Recent:** The City of Grand Rapids officially launched its 2027 Parks and Recreation Master Plan process, seeking public input to shape the future of parks, trails, recreation programs, and green spaces.
 (City of Grand Rapids, 2026)

- 
**Upcoming fall 2026:** Canal Park is slated to reopen downtown with a new universally accessible, river-themed playscape, a barrier-free canoe/kayak launch, and river overlooks.
 
Johnson Park will also open a new natural-surface trail for biking, hiking, running, and adaptive cycling in fall 2026.
 (Experience Grand Rapids, 2026)

entries.title: Regulations and advisories
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or recently confirmed updates for the River Brain, all from within the last ~30 days or representing status changes since the August 1, 2026 base research date:

---

- 
**Grand River dam removal construction began July 2, 2026:** After 18 years of planning, construction crews entered the river to begin removing four low-head dams from the downtown Grand Rapids stretch.
 (Spectrum News)

- 
**Construction contract awarded February 2026:** The City of Grand Rapids issued a contract to Taplin Inc. for $14,562,625.98, with total expenditures capped at $25,982,101.
 
The Lower Reach phase covers Fulton Street to Bridge Street and includes dam removal to eliminate dangerous hydraulics and improve public safety.
 (Grand Rapids WhiteWater, Experience GR)

- 
**Sea lamprey barrier funding secured:** Over $20 million in federal funding for a new lamprey barrier in the Grand River has been identified and committed to the Great Lakes Fishery Commission.
 (Grand Rapids WhiteWater)

- 
**MDHHS 2026 Eat Safe Fish Guides released June 8, 2026**, covering fish consumption recommendations for waters statewide including the Grand River corridor.
 
Statewide, 59 guidelines were relaxed and 65 became more protective compared to the prior year.
 (MDHHS, WNEM)

- No new Grand River-specific E. coli or public health contact advisories for the Grand Rapids/Kent County reach were found for July–August 2026. The Kent County Health Department's most recent public alert concerned Jamestown Canyon virus in mosquitoes in ZIP code 49504, not a river water-quality advisory. (Kent County Health Department)

- 
**DNR 2026 fishing regulations in effect April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2027** include no Grand River-specific rule changes; the headline sturgeon regulation change applies to the Menominee River (Grand Rapids Dam to Sturgeon Falls Dam), not the Grand River in Grand Rapids.
 (Michigan DNR) **Note for River Brain:** Confirm that no Grand River-specific DNR regulation changes were enacted for 2026, as search results confirm no such changes.

entries.title: Events and community
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (relative to the Aug 3, 2026 base date), plus the most recent prior-month items that are clearly new since any earlier River Brain compilation:

---

- 
**Dam removal active in river, July 1, 2026:** In-river construction began July 1 to remove four low-head dams between Bridge Street Bridge and Fulton Street Bridge; the start date was set by regulatory requirements to protect fish spawning and prevent sea lamprey movement past Sixth Street Dam. (City of Grand Rapids)


- 
**Active construction confirmed, July 1-2, 2026:** After 18 years of planning, equipment entered the river; Grand Rapids WhiteWater Executive Director Matt Chapman stated crews expect "rapids back in Grand Rapids" within two years. (Spectrum Local News)


- 
**Ah-Nab-Awen Park closed for project duration, May 18, 2026 onward:** Crews began staging equipment and materials on May 18; the closure of Ah-Nab-Awen Park is in effect through the project period. (City of Grand Rapids PublicInput)


- 
**Grand River Edges Trail, Leonard to Ann, groundbreaking June 15, 2026:** Leaders and state officials gathered June 15 to mark the groundbreaking of the 0.75-mile, 12-foot-wide multi-use trail segment running along the river between Leonard Street and Ann Street NW. (Grand Rapids Magazine)


- 
**Edges Trail construction past halfway, June 17, 2026:** Construction was already underway and approaching its halfway point at the time of the groundbreaking ceremony; once complete, the trail will close the gap linking downtown to Riverside Park and the Fred Meijer White Pine Trail. (Grand Rapids Magazine)


- 
**Return to the River Festival 2026 date confirmed, August 22-23, 2026:** The free, DGRI-produced music and art festival is scheduled for August 22 and 23 in Downtown Grand Rapids. (Return to the River Instagram)

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from approximately the last 30 days (since ~July 3, 2026) and the most relevant recent developments since base research on August 1, 2026:

---

- **Grand River Restoration Lower Reach construction underway, July 1, 2026:** 
After 18 years of planning, crews entered the river July 1 to begin removing four low-head dams; the July 1 start date was set by state permit to ensure the Sixth Street Dam's water levels continue blocking invasive sea lamprey during construction.
 
Lower reach construction is expected to be completed by end of 2027.
 (Spectrum News / WWMT, July 2, 2026)

- **Snuffbox mussel relocation underway as part of dam removal, 2026:** 
The total project budget includes "2026 mussel relocation by BioSurvey Group" and fish relocation by Encompass Socio-Ecological Consulting
 as required conservation measures prior to and during construction. 
The Lower Reach will enhance aquatic habitat across 2,887 feet and 30 acres of river corridor, including improved habitat for lake sturgeon, river redhorse, and snuffbox mussel.
 (Grand Rapids WhiteWater / ExperienceGR, June–July 2026)

- **Sea lamprey 2026 control season active Great Lakes-wide, July 24, 2026:** 
Between April and November 2026, crews are applying lampricides TFM and Bayluscide to streams and still-water areas across the Great Lakes where young sea lamprey are present, with treatments highly effective at reducing larval numbers before they migrate.
 
This year's Canadian program covers tributaries on Lake Superior, Lake Huron, and Lake Ontario.
 (Sydenham Current / Great Lakes Commission, July 24, 2026)

- **Lake sturgeon research 2026 funded by Great Lakes Fishery Trust:** 
Funding for Grand River sturgeon research in 2026 is provided by the Great Lakes Fishery Trust, with the collaborative team including GRPM, John Ball Zoo, GVSU, Encompass Consulting, MDNR, and USFWS.
 (Grand Rapids Public Museum, 2026)

- **New Michigan state-record gizzard shad caught in Grand River, April 22, 2026:** 
An angler from Lowell, Michigan, caught a new state-record gizzard shad weighing 4.45 pounds and measuring 20.3 inches long, while spincasting on the Grand River in Kent County on April 22.
 
This beat the previous record of 4.12 pounds set in 1996 on Lake St. Clair.
 (Michigan DNR, May 7, 2026)

- **Invasive lesser celandine plant widely established in Grand River corridor:** 
According to the Michigan DNR, the invasive plant lesser celandine is already widely established along the Grand River corridor and is actively spreading in lower Michigan and southeastern Wisconsin.
 
Several partner organizations have formed the Michigan Lesser Celandine Coalition, recruiting volunteers to assess its spread

entries.title: Hydrology and weather
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or recently updated findings for the River Brain, covering roughly the past 30 days (early July through August 3, 2026):

---

- 
**Low gage height, Aug 1, 2026:** USGS gauge 04119000 (Grand River at Grand Rapids) recorded a provisional gage height of **1.16 ft** at 8:00 PM EDT on August 1, 2026, well below the 12 ft action stage. (USGS Water Data for the Nation)


- 
**Statewide drought footprint, Jul 21, 2026:** Michigan's active drought covered approximately 2% of the state (1,479 sq mi), with 0.8% (742 sq mi) in Moderate Drought (D1) and 0.8% (737 sq mi) in Severe Drought (D2), plus an additional 5% classified Abnormally Dry (D0). (PlantMaps / U.S. Drought Monitor)


- 
**NWS gauge status, late July 2026:** No flood watches, warnings, or advisories were in effect at the Grand River at North Park St, Grand Rapids gauge as of the most recent NWS check. (NOAA National Water Prediction Service)


- 
**Dam removal construction launched, Jul 1, 2026:** The Grand River Restoration project entered active in-water construction on July 1, 2026, with crews moving between the Bridge Street and Fulton Street bridges to begin removing four low-head dams. (Grand Rapids Magazine)


- 
**Precipitation deficit at Grand Rapids, as of Aug 2, 2026:** NWS Grand Rapids climate data shows Grand Rapids recorded only 4.73 inches since June 1, against a normal of 7.80 inches, a shortfall of 3.07 inches. Year-to-date precipitation of 24.10 inches remains slightly above the 22.82-inch normal. (NWS Grand Rapids Daily Climate)


- 
**2026 National Hydrologic Assessment released:** NOAA posted its 2026 National Hydrologic Assessment, now linked from all Grand River gauge pages. No Grand River-specific findings are publicly excerpted in the search results. (NOAA National Water Prediction Service)

entries.title: Construction progress
entries.body:
Now let me do one more targeted search to check for any very recent news from the last 30 days (July 2026 to Aug 3, 2026) specifically.
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (July 2026 through Aug 3, 2026), with notes where slightly older milestones from the research window are included because they represent state changes not previously captured in the River Brain base:

---

- **Lower Reach in-river construction started July 1, 2026.** 
The July 1 start date was set by state regulatory requirements to protect fish spawning periods and prevent sea lamprey from moving past the Sixth Street Dam; contractor Taplin Group opened by installing turbidity curtains in the river.
 
Over the following weeks, crews began building causeways for equipment access, and a cofferdam was installed to isolate a section of Dam 2 for the first boulder arch feature.
 (Spectrum News / City of Grand Rapids, July 1-2, 2026)

- **Ah-Nab-Awen Park confirmed closed for approximately two years.** 
Equipment staging began May 18, and the resulting Ah-Nab-Awen Park closure will continue through the full project period.
 
The park remains closed during this phase; the Gillett Bridge stays open.
 (City of Grand Rapids PublicInput, updated July 2026)

- **Active construction season runs July through mid-October or early November 2026.** 
Trucks and heavy equipment will be moving rocks and boulders in and out of the flowing river channel throughout the construction season, which runs roughly July through mid-October or early November each year, weather and river conditions permitting.
 Second construction season is anticipated for summer 2027. (Spectrum News, July 2, 2026)

- **Upper Reach EIS scoping comment period closed May 22, 2026; draft EIS now targeted for July 2027.** 
The EIS process, originally paused after 2019, was officially resumed by the Great Lakes Fishery Commission and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in spring 2026; a public scoping meeting was held April 22 and the 30-day comment period closed May 22; a draft EIS is anticipated in July 2027.
 (Grand Rapids WhiteWater, grandrapidswhitewater.org)

- **Army Corps of Engineers confirmed it is preparing the EIS for Sixth Street Dam removal and a replacement sea lamprey barrier.** 
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Detroit District is preparing an Environmental Impact Statement to evaluate removal of the 6th Street Dam and construction of a sea lamprey barrier on the Grand River in Grand Rapids.
 
Two barrier design alternatives are under consideration: a fixed crest design similar to the current dam, or an adjustable barrier dam.
 (U.S. Army Corps of Engineers / WZZM13, April 2026)

- **Over $20 million in federal funding committed to the new lamprey barrier for the Upper Reach.** 
More than $20 million in federal funding for a new lamprey barrier in the Grand River has been identified and committed to the Great Lakes Fishery Commission, sourced from Great Lakes Restoration Initiative funding and a GLFC annual budget appropriation.
 (Grand Rapids WhiteWater, grandrapidswhitewater.org)

entries.title: History and culture
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or recently changed items relevant to the River Brain, all from within approximately the last 30 days or otherwise newly surfaced in 2026:

---

- **New book published, Jan. 13, 2026:** 
*The Historical Archaeology of Michigan* by Dean L. Anderson, Michael S. Nassaney, and Krysta Ryzewski was published by University Press of Florida on January 13, 2026 (280 pages).
 
The book covers the past 400 years of Michigan history through archaeological themes of entrepreneurship, immigration, capitalism, and civil rights, including chapters on European colonization, the fur trade, and 19th-century logging.
 (JSTOR / University Press of Florida)

- **Federal recognition bill reintroduced in House, May 8, 2025, Senate companion June 26, 2025:** 
U.S. Rep. Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03) reintroduced the bipartisan Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians Restoration Act alongside Rep. John James (R-MI-10) on May 8, 2025.
 
Senators Elissa Slotkin and Gary Peters introduced companion Senate legislation on June 26, 2025.
 
The Grand River Bands are described as the last treaty tribe east of the Mississippi River without federal recognition.
 (Scholten House press release / Slotkin Senate press release)

- **H.R. 3255 in active 119th Congress:** 
The Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians Restoration Act of 2025 (H.R. 3255) formally affirms federal recognition of the tribe and makes members eligible for services and benefits provided to federally recognized tribes, regardless of reservation status.
 
The designated service area spans Newaygo, Oceana, Kent, Muskegon, and Ottawa Counties in Michigan.
 (Congress.gov)

- **GRPM "Ice Age: Michigan's Frozen Secrets" exhibit, open as of July 2026:** 
*Ice Age: Michigan's Frozen Secrets* and *Snow: Tiny Crystals, Global Impact* are now open at the Grand Rapids Public Museum.
 
The Ice Age exhibit explores North America during the last glacial period, featuring real Ice Age fossils including bones from the recently discovered "Clapp Family Mastodon."
 (Grand Rapids Public Museum)

- **GRPM Anishinaabe Star Knowledge planetarium show, active summer 2026:** 
The GRPM is currently featuring planetarium shows including *Anishinaabe Star Knowledge*, alongside *Secrets of the Sun* and *Dinosaurs: A Story of Survival*.
 (Grand Rapids Public Museum)

entries.title: Development and funding
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or recently changed items for the River Brain, all from approximately the last 30 days or items not yet captured as of August 1, 2026:

---

- 
**Michigan Transformational Brownfield Program reformed, July 22, 2026:** Gov. Whitmer signed SB 723 into law as Public Act 36 of 2026, revising the state's Transformational Brownfield Program by expanding oversight, increasing transparency, and tying state tax reimbursements to measurable project performance.
 
The law doubles the post-construction tax capture cap from $1.6 billion to $3.2 billion, taking effect immediately.
 
State officials cited stalled riverfront work in Grand Rapids as a key example of the capacity constraints the law is meant to relieve.
 (July 22, 2026, Environment+Energy Leader / Crain's Grand Rapids Business)

- 
**Fulton & Market towers incentive capacity unlocked, mid-July 2026:** Major waterfront developments in Grand Rapids, Muskegon, and Holland are expected to benefit from the expanded Transformational Brownfield Program.
 
The Grand Rapids riverfront towers had stalled as state incentives ran dry, with developers saying progress depended on lawmakers restoring key state incentives.
 (July 14–22, 2026, Crain's Grand Rapids Business)

- 
**Former Naval Reserve Center riverfront site auctioned, May 20, 2026:** The GSA formally listed the former Navy and Marine Corps Reserve Center in Grand Rapids for public purchase; the nearly 3.47-acre parcel contains four buildings totaling 48,120 square feet.
 
GSA Administrator Edward Forst stated the sale "will save taxpayers nearly $350,000 in annual operating costs and $27 million in cost avoidance."
 (May 20, 2026, GSA.gov)

- 
**Parks department acquires 6 land-bank lots for trails and green space, May 2026:** The Grand Rapids Parks and Recreation Department acquired six lots from the land bank, deemed unbuildable for housing, and is making plans for trails and green space as part of its network.
 (May 11, 2026, Crain's Grand Rapids Business)

- 
**New brownfield hearings scheduled for July 21, 2026:** Grand Rapids officials considered tax incentives for two projects, including a nearly 100,000-square-foot industrial facility; both had received preliminary approval from the Brownfield Redevelopment Authority, with public hearings scheduled for July 21.
 
Profile Films sought a brownfield plan amendment to be reimbursed for about $5 million in eligible activities, plus an industrial development district designation and a 12-year industrial facilities exemption certificate.
 (June 19 / July 2026, WOOD TV / Yahoo News)

entries.title: Regulations and advisories
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items found within approximately the last 30 days (relative to August 2, 2026):

---

- 
**Grand River dam removal construction began July 1, 2026:** After 18 years of planning, in-river construction commenced on July 1 to remove four low-head dams from downtown Grand Rapids. The July 1 start date aligns with state regulatory requirements protecting fish spawning periods and preventing sea lamprey movement past the Sixth Street Dam.
 (City of Grand Rapids / Spectrum News)

- 
**Two-year construction timeline confirmed:** Over the next two years, the four lower-reach dams will be removed and replaced with boulder arch structures, constructed riffles, and scattered habitat boulders. Construction is expected to be completed by end of 2027, weather and river conditions permitting.
 (WWMT / City of Grand Rapids)

- 
**Contractor and first work scope identified:** The Taplin Group is the city's contractor for the lower-reach project and is building causeways in the coming weeks to allow construction equipment to travel safely in the river, plus a cofferdam to isolate a section of Dam 2 for the boulder arch feature.
 (City of Grand Rapids)

- 
**MDHHS 2026 Eat Safe Fish Guides released June 8, 2026:** MDHHS published updated consumption guidelines covering 696 Michigan waterbodies, including Southwest Michigan waters covering the Grand River corridor. Statewide, 59 guidelines were relaxed and 65 became more protective compared to prior year.
 (MDHHS / WNEM)

- 
**Federal USDA funding of $11,026,695 confirmed March 23, 2026** for the lower Grand River restoration covering an approximately 2,887-foot stretch through downtown Grand Rapids, channeled through the USDA to improve public safety, restore aquatic habitat for native Great Lakes fish and mussel species, and enhance river access.
 (Rep. Hillary Scholten press release)

No new Grand River-specific EGLE permit actions or public health (E. coli/contact) advisories for the Grand River in Kent County were found within the last 30 days. The most recent public health advisory on record for this stretch remains prior to August 2026.

entries.title: Events and community
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since approximately July 2, 2026):

---

- **In-river dam removal construction started July 1, 2026:** 
After 18 years of planning, crews entered the water on July 1 to begin removing four low-head dams from downtown, a date aligned with state regulatory requirements protecting fish spawning periods.
 
The lower reach is expected to be completed by end of 2027; the first near-term task is installing scour protection around Gillett Bridge piers before placing a cofferdam to isolate a section for construction of the first boulder arch structure.
 (July 1, 2026, Spectrum News / WOODTV)

- **Return to the River Festival 2026 dates set, Aug 22-23:** 
DGRI's Instagram confirmed the festival is scheduled for August 22 and 23, 2026, as a free music and art festival in downtown Grand Rapids.
 
The festival will span three Riverwalk locations: 555 Monroe, Sixth Street Park, and Canal Park in downtown Grand Rapids, all connected and within walking distance.
 (DGRI Instagram, circa July 2026)

- **Grand River Edges' Trail extension groundbreaking, June 15, 2026:** 
Construction started on a new Greenway extension between Leonard Street NW and Ann Street NW near downtown Grand Rapids; the segment, called the Grand River Edges' Trail, will be three-quarters of a mile long and will eventually include street crossings, lighting, benches, and native plants.
 
The trail extension is expected to be complete by the end of 2026.
 (WOODTV, June 15, 2026)

- **GRPM Grand River Adventure event announced for Aug 15, 2026:** 
The Grand Rapids Public Museum announced its 4th annual Grand River Adventure for August 15, 2026, celebrating the history, science, culture, art, and stewardship of the Grand River Watershed.
 
The one-day, open-house style event invites families and community members on an immersive journey through the river's past, present, and future, with a focus on watershed preservation.
 (GRPM website, current listing)

- **Upper Reach EIS public comment closed May 22, 2026:** 
The Environmental Impact Study process for the Upper Reach (Sixth Street Dam) is currently underway; the public comment period closed May 22, 2026, and a construction timeline will not be available until the EIS process is complete and a permittable design is finalized.
 (Grand Rapids Whitewater, updated June 2026)

- **Grand River gage height very low as of Aug 1, 2026:** 
USGS monitoring recorded a gage height of 1.16 ft at the Grand River at Grand Rapids as of August 1, 2026 at 8:00 PM EDT, provisional data.
 This is notably low and relevant to in-river construction conditions. (USGS Water Data, Aug 1, 2026)

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed findings from roughly the last 30 days (and the most recent weeks of the broader July 2026 window), relevant to the Grand River Brain reference model:

---

- **Dam removal and habitat construction underway, July 1, 2026:** 
After 18 years of planning, in-river construction began July 1, 2026, with crews removing four low-head dams from downtown Grand Rapids. The July 1 start date was set by state regulatory requirements to protect fish spawning periods and prevent invasive sea lamprey from moving past the Sixth Street Dam.
 (Spectrum Local News / City of Grand Rapids)

- **Sea lamprey barrier EIS process active, Sixth Street Dam design timeline set:** 
The Great Lakes Fishery Commission and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers officially resumed the Upper Reach Environmental Impact Statement process in spring 2026. A public scoping meeting was held April 22, 2026, with a 30-day comment period closing May 22, 2026. A draft EIS is anticipated in July 2027.
 Separately, 
GLFC aquatic connectivity coordinator Lisa Walter stated: "We're looking at probably 2028 until we have a project design selected."
 (Bridge Michigan / Grand Rapids Whitewater)

- **Snuffbox mussel relocation completed prior to construction:** 
Relocation of threatened and endangered mussel species, including snuffbox, was required and completed prior to the July 1 in-river construction start. The project design reduced impacts to endangered mussels to the greatest extent possible, and pre-construction relocation was determined to have the most ecological benefit for these species.
 (Grand Rapids Whitewater)

- **Lake sturgeon research funding for 2026 shifted to Great Lakes Fishery Trust:** 
Funding for Grand River lake sturgeon research in 2026 is provided by the Great Lakes Fishery Trust
, a change from prior U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service GLFWRA grants. (Grand Rapids Public Museum)

- **New Michigan state-record gizzard shad caught in Grand River, April 22, 2026:** 
Sedrick Neinhuis was fishing on the Grand River on April 22, 2026, and landed a new state-record gizzard shad weighing 4.45 pounds and measuring 20.3 inches, surpassing the previous record of 4.12 pounds set on Lake St. Clair in 1996.
 (Michigan DNR / WGRD)

- **Six invasive plant species added to Michigan's prohibited/restricted lists, effective June 19, 2026:** 
The Michigan Commission of Agriculture and Rural Development voted on May 20, 2026, to add callery pear, common buckthorn, glossy buckthorn, Japanese barberry, water hyacinth, and water lettuce to Michigan's prohibited and restricted plant lists.
 Several of these (water hyacinth, water lettuce) are aquatic and relevant to Grand River watershed monitoring. (Michigan Invasive Species Program)

entries.title: Hydrology and weather
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed findings from roughly the last 30 days (since ~July 3, 2026). Note that the major spring flood event (April 2026) is already prior documented history for the River Brain; only items below are newly surfaced or represent a change in status.

---

- **No active flood watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect at the Grand River at Grand Rapids gauge (GDRM4) as of July 28, 2026**, the most recent NWS update. 
The NOAA gauge page shows no watches, warnings, or advisories in effect, last updated July 28, 2026.


- **Michigan drought conditions have eased substantially by late July 2026.** 
As of July 21, 2026, only about 2% of Michigan (approximately 1,479 square miles) is under active drought, with 0.8% (742 sq mi) in moderate drought (D1) and 0.8% (737 sq mi) in severe drought (D2).
 This is a sharp improvement from the 34%+ drought coverage documented in fall 2025.

- **River flow at Grand Rapids is running well below seasonal normal in early July 2026.** 
The gauge at Grand Rapids was flowing at approximately 2,280 cfs at 2.15 ft, down 9% day-over-day, with a 10-day average of 2,841 cfs peaking at 3,180 cfs, and forecast to recede to roughly 2,092 cfs by July 6, running well below seasonal normal.
 (Note: this snapshot appears to be from early July 2026 per the Snoflo forecast date.)

- **Grand Rapids precipitation is running 2.05 inches below normal for July 2026 month-to-date as of August 1.** 
NWS climate data shows July month-to-date precipitation at 1.81 inches versus a normal of 3.86 inches, a deficit of 2.05 inches, while year-to-date precipitation of 24.10 inches is 1.28 inches above the annual normal of 22.82 inches.


- **A separate July 2026 Michigan flood emergency does not affect the Grand River basin directly.** 
On July 9, 2026, Governor Whitmer declared a state of emergency for Antrim, Cheboygan, and Emmet counties following an intense rainstorm on June 29, 2026, which severely damaged roads and infrastructure
, all of which are in northern Michigan well outside the Grand River watershed.
